entries.subject: A surface map of Luhman 16 A
entries.finding: Chen et al. (2024) performed multi-band Doppler imaging of the Luhman 16 AB system (as Ureshino et al. 2026 summarise it), but no map of A is deposited or used here. The sphere stays neutral gray.
entries.revisitWhen: A map of Luhman 16 A is deposited with its paper.

entries.subject: The color of Luhman 16 A
entries.finding: Faherty et al. (2014) published resolved MagE optical spectra of A and B, archived in the SIMPLE database; the color dataset is taken from A's. A blackbody color would have been wrong: the spectrum is dominated by sodium and potassium absorption.

entries.subject: The hue of Luhman 16 A below 650 nm
entries.finding: Below 650 nm the dwarf is so faint that single pixels of the MagE spectrum have a signal-to-noise ratio near 1. Moving the whole spectrum one standard error down or up gives #ff005e to #ff52c6, from red-pink to lilac.
entries.revisitWhen: A resolved optical spectrum with higher signal below 650 nm is published.

entries.subject: Placing Luhman 16 A itself rather than the barycentre
entries.finding: Bedin et al. (2024) give the barycentre's astrometry; A sits at 0.4535 of the separation from it, up to 1.6 au. A is drawn at the barycentre and B circles A.
entries.revisitWhen: The world frame can place a binary's components around their barycentre.

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law (u1 0.46, u2 0) de Regt et al. (2025), The ESO SupJup Survey VII, A&A 696, A225 fit to this star (VLT/CRIRES+ J1226 setting (1.1-1.4 um); not a visible band). Gravity: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/luhman-16.json: 4.935.
